regulatory_notes: Verify state commercial-purpose lending exemptions, usury ceilings and escrow licensing rules.
Release funds strictly to bonded title/settlement agents after verifying unconditional end-buyer cash on deposit.

plays.name: 24-to-72-Hour Escrow-Locked Transactional ("Flash") Double-Close Funding
plays.mechanism: Fund the A->B acquisition only after the title agent independently verifies cleared, unconditional end-buyer B->C funds in escrow and an enforceable closing waterfall. Target a 1.0%–2.5% earned funding fee per 1–3 day turn; closing delays, fraud and legal restrictions can impair returns or principal.
inputs: Executed A->B and B->C purchase contracts, title commitment and independently verified settlement-agent credentials
Cleared end-buyer escrow funds, written disbursement conditions and a reconciled same-transaction payoff waterfall
Commercial-purpose funding agreement reviewed for applicable licensing, usury and escrow requirements
workflow: 1. Underwrite both contracts, title exceptions, end-buyer closing conditions and the settlement agent's authority and applicable bonding or insurance.
2. Independently confirm end-buyer cleared funds and irrevocable disbursement instructions using a previously verified title-agent contact channel.
3. Wire A->B funding only to approved title escrow after all release conditions are satisfied and the closing sequence is documented.
4. Reconcile B->C settlement, recover principal and earned fees, and release capital for reuse only after cleared repayment is confirmed.
metrics: Earned funding fees as a percentage of funded principal per completed turn
Median and maximum hours from funding disbursement to cleared repayment
Unrecovered principal and delayed-closing exposure as a percentage of outstanding funding

platform_risks.failure_mode: Fraudulent wire instructions or conditional end-buyer funds leave the A->B advance unrepaid
platform_risks.trigger: Last-minute beneficiary changes, failed independent callbacks or unresolved B->C release conditions
platform_risks.impact: Loss of principal, prolonged escrow disputes and interruption of capital recycling
platform_risks.detection_metric: Count of unresolved wire-verification exceptions and funded closings past contractual repayment deadlines
platform_risks.fallback: Stop disbursement, independently reverify settlement instructions and obtain counsel-directed escrow recovery before further funding

plays.name: Earnest-Money Deposit ("Gator") Escrow Lending & Joint-Venture Splits
plays.mechanism: Advance $2,500–$25,000 refundable-contingency earnest-money deposits directly to title escrow under documented JV or promissory protections, with security recorded or perfected where legally appropriate. Negotiate a 15%–30% share of an earned assignment fee or a lawful fixed return; refunds depend on contractual deadlines, valid contingency exercise and escrow release terms.
inputs: Assignable purchase agreement with explicit refundable contingencies, notice procedures and deadline calendar
Verified title escrow account and executed JV or promissory documents with legally appropriate recorded or perfected protections
Borrower diligence, assignment economics and state-specific lending, brokerage, securities and usury review
workflow: 1. Verify assignment rights, counterparty identity, refundable contingencies and the enforceability of the proposed JV or lending structure.
2. Execute repayment and profit-split documents, perfect any lawful security and transmit the deposit directly to verified title escrow.
3. Track contingency and assignment deadlines, require documented progress and deliver timely cancellation notices when authorized and necessary.
4. Reconcile the closing or refund statement, recover deposited principal and collect only the contractually earned fee or lawful return.
metrics: Earned assignment-fee share or fixed return per completed deposit advance
Percentage of active deposits with verified unexpired refund rights and complete documentation
Deposit loss rate and median days from advance to cleared repayment

platform_risks.failure_mode: A supposedly refundable deposit becomes nonrefundable or disputed
platform_risks.trigger: Missed contingency notice deadline, invalid cancellation or unauthorized contract amendment
platform_risks.impact: Deposit forfeiture, delayed recovery and disputes over assignment proceeds
platform_risks.detection_metric: Deposits approaching contingency expiry without documented assignment or cancellation instructions
platform_risks.fallback: Freeze additional advances, seek timely authorized cancellation and pursue counsel-reviewed escrow release or contractual remedies

plays.name: Aged Shelf-Corp Reinstatement, Primary Tradeline & 0%-APR Corporate Credit Stacking
plays.mechanism: Compare reinstated entities and genuine business credit facilities for working-capital financing; entity age is not operating history, and promotional APR economics require accurate underwriting and repayment capacity.
inputs: Entity filings, beneficial ownership, and liability searches
Verified operating financials and genuine supplier tradelines
Lender eligibility, promotional APR, fee, and guarantee terms
workflow: 1. Audit the entity's ownership, tax liabilities, and reinstatement requirements
2. Disclose acquisition and actual operating history; establish only genuine paid supplier accounts
3. Compare lender-approved applications with full debt disclosure and consolidated exposure limits
4. Fund documented business expenses and repay before promotional expiry using cash-flow reserves
metrics: Effective borrowing cost including fees
Debt service coverage under post-promotion APR
Utilization and days to promotional expiry

platform_risks.failure_mode: Credit withdrawal or unaffordable repricing
platform_risks.trigger: Misstated operating history, undisclosed debt, or expired promotional terms
platform_risks.impact: Account closure, accelerated repayment, and guarantee exposure
platform_risks.detection_metric: Underwriting discrepancies and stressed repayment coverage
platform_risks.fallback: Halt applications, correct disclosures, and use a transparent term facility or reduce financed spending

plays.name: B2B Commercial Virtual Card (VCC) Interchange & AP Settlement Rebate Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Embedding a 'Free Automated Accounts Payable (AP) / Instant Vendor Settlement' platform inside high-volume B2B verticals (freight brokerage, construction general contracting, medical supply, property management, media agencies) that converts checks and ACH payables into single-use Visa/Mastercard Commercial Virtual Credit Cards (VCCs)—capturing 140–195 basis points (1.40%–1.95%) in uncapped commercial interchange rebates on hundreds of millions in third-party invoice volume.
inputs: BaaS / Commercial Card Issuing bank partnership (Marqeta, Lithic, Stripe Issuing, Highnote, Cross River) on uncapped Visa/Mastercard Large-Ticket & Purchasing interchange tiers
ERP/accounting connector (QuickBooks, NetSuite, Sage, McLeod/TMW freight TMS) ingesting open vendor AP ledgers
Automated vendor-enablement call/email engine pitching 'Day-1 Instant Payment via Virtual Card vs. Net-45 Check/ACH'
workflow: Onboard mid-market companies with $20M–$250M/yr in fragmented vendor payables onto a $0-cost AP automation and working-capital portal
Cross-reference their vendor master list against Visa/Mastercard supplier-acceptance networks to flag vendors that already accept card payments
Offer remaining vendors immediate Day-1 invoice settlement via single-use emailed/API virtual card in exchange for waiving Net-30/Net-60 wait times
Earn 1.50%–1.95% gross interchange rebate from the issuing bank on every settled dollar, sharing 0.25%–0.50% with the corporate client while retaining 1.10%–1.45% net platform margin
metrics: Total annualized Gross Payment Volume (GPV $) converted from ACH/check to Virtual Card (target: 25–45% of total AP)
Net retained interchange spread in basis points (110–145 bps) after bank processor fees and client revenue share
Vendor card-acceptance retention rate (%) across repeat monthly invoices

platform_risks.failure_mode: Vendor card-surcharging pushback or Visa/Mastercard Level-2/Level-3 large-ticket interchange downgrade
platform_risks.trigger: Large vendors refusing card settlement or failing to pass Level-3 line-item tax/invoice metadata with the authorization
platform_risks.impact: Shift of specific vendors back to low-margin ACH or interchange rate step-down
platform_risks.detection_metric: Automated Level-2/Level-3 data-enrichment pass rate and per-vendor surcharge detection
platform_risks.fallback: Automatically inject Level-3 line-item invoice metadata at card creation, offer dynamic early-pay ACH discounts (1.5%–2% 10-day net) for card-averse vendors, and focus on fragmented long-tail vendor bases

plays.name: Whitelisted Agency Ad-Spend Card-Multiplier Points & Volume-Rebate Cycling
plays.mechanism: Route genuine client-authorized advertising spend through eligible agency payment arrangements to earn contract-permitted rewards and volume rebates, net of financing, processing, and client pass-through obligations.
inputs: Client media mandates and rebate ownership clauses
Issuer reward categories, caps, and repayment terms
Platform invoices and agency volume-rebate agreements
workflow: 1. Verify client authorization, platform payment permissions, and ownership of rewards and rebates
2. Model eligible media purchases against reward caps, fees, liquidity, and rebate thresholds
3. Pay only genuine approved advertising invoices without circular spend or fabricated transactions
4. Reconcile settled rewards, client credits, refunds, and full card repayment each statement cycle
metrics: Net retained rewards and rebates per media dollar
Unfunded client exposure and repayment coverage
Invoice-to-reward reconciliation variance

platform_risks.failure_mode: Reward clawback or client-funded liquidity shortfall
platform_risks.trigger: Ineligible categories, prohibited payment aggregation, or delayed client reimbursement
platform_risks.impact: Lost rebates, interest costs, and card suspension
platform_risks.detection_metric: Denied reward value and overdue client balances versus cash reserves
platform_risks.fallback: Move to client-direct billing or prefunded approved agency terms and stop rewards-dependent spending

plays.name: UCC-1 Filing, MCA Stacking & Maturity-Date Trigger Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Monitor state Secretary of State UCC-1 financing statements and continuation filings to identify operating businesses 4–9 months into high-cost Merchant Cash Advances (MCAs) or equipment notes, triggering refinance and debt-consolidation live transfers.
inputs: Daily state SOS UCC-1 initial, amendment, & termination bulk feeds
Secured-party lender dictionary (identifying MCA vs. bank/SBA filings)
Live-transfer commercial refinance & SBA consolidation desk
workflow: Classify daily UCC-1 filings by secured party to isolate businesses that took high-cost short-term working capital 120–240 days ago
Enrich business owner direct phone and email and score by industry revenue stability
Contact merchants during peak renewal/payoff windows to offer lower-rate term consolidation or equipment refinancing, monetizing via broker points or live-transfer fees
metrics: UCC-to-verified-decision-maker match rate (%)
Live-transfer qualification rate (%)
Origination commission / referral fee per funded refi

platform_risks.failure_mode: TCPA automated-calling liability or state commercial-financing disclosure violations
platform_risks.trigger: Robocalling cell phones without consent or quoting misleading APRs in states with commercial Truth-in-Lending laws (CA, NY, UT, VA)
platform_risks.impact: Statutory TCPA demand letters or state DFPI regulatory enforcement
platform_risks.detection_metric: 100% DNC/litigator-scrub pass rate and statutory APR disclosure audit in regulated states
platform_risks.fallback: Use direct mail, B2B work-email sequences, and manual human-dialed outreach paired with compliant state commercial financing disclosures

plays.name: MCA UCC-1 Trigger Stacking & Dual-Sided Default-Restructure Brokerage
plays.mechanism: Use UCC filing changes to identify businesses that may need cash-flow review and consensual MCA restructuring, with verified obligations and disclosed compensation rather than encouraging undisclosed stacking.
inputs: Public UCC filings and termination records
Merchant-authorized contracts and cash-flow statements
Broker licensing rules and disclosed creditor compensation terms
workflow: 1. Treat UCC changes as outreach signals, not proof of default, and obtain merchant authorization
2. Reconcile advances, liens, repayment pulls, covenants, and sustainable payment capacity
3. Disclose dual-sided fees and conflicts; use independent counsel where representation would conflict
4. Coordinate documented creditor-approved modifications and monitor actual payment relief
metrics: Net merchant payment relief after fees
Creditor-approved modification rate
Post-restructure missed-payment rate

platform_risks.failure_mode: Conflicted brokerage or prohibited stacking worsens default
platform_risks.trigger: Hidden commissions, inaccurate balances, or new financing breaching existing contracts
platform_risks.impact: Accelerated collections and broker liability
platform_risks.detection_metric: Undisclosed fee exceptions and covenant breaches per engagement
platform_risks.fallback: Stop placement, refund improper fees, and refer the merchant to independent licensed restructuring counsel

plays.name: Public-Record & API Intelligence
plays.mechanism: Ingest fragmented county dockets, probate registries, unclaimed property ledgers, and public APIs to surface uncontested claims or high-intent B2B triggers before manual competitors.
inputs: Court & probate dockets
State controller ledgers
Public licensing & entity APIs
workflow: Poll and normalize county/state record releases on an automated cadence
Cross-match entity/kinship/lien records and filter by minimum net fee threshold
Route verified dossiers into compliant outreach and claim execution
metrics: Cost per verified lead
Docket-to-contact latency (hours)
Net recovery / conversion rate

platform_risks.failure_mode: Portal rate-limiting or CAPTCHA gating
platform_risks.trigger: High-frequency automated polling against county or agency web portals
platform_risks.impact: Delayed lead ingestion or temporary IP block on target registry
platform_risks.detection_metric: HTTP 429/403 rate and daily record ingestion delta
platform_risks.fallback: Switch to scheduled bulk FOIA/public-record exports, official data feeds, and low-frequency cached queues

plays.name: New-LLC & Recorded-Deed Trigger-Mail Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Ingest daily Secretary of State new-LLC filings and County Recorder new-deed/mortgage recordings to trigger programmatic direct mail via API—replacing illegal government-lookalike poster/deed invoices (which violate 39 U.S.C. § 3001 and state deed-solicitation laws) with high-LTV recurring workplace compliance subscriptions, property-tax appeal contingency offers, and exclusive new-mover/B2B lead monetization.
inputs: Daily Secretary of State new-entity (LLC/Corp) bulk feeds
County Recorder grant/warranty deed & mortgage recording dockets
Programmatic print-and-mail API (Lob / PostGrid) + QR intake bridge
workflow: Pull daily new-LLC formations (filtering for employer/commercial NAICS or multi-member filings) and newly recorded residential deeds with purchase price and loan metadata
Dispatch transparent, non-governmental trigger mailers within 24–48 hours of filing with personalized QR codes pre-populating entity or parcel data

Monetize new LLCs via recurring annual labor-poster/registered-agent compliance memberships and B2B partner referrals; monetize new deeds via contingency property-tax appeal filings or high-ticket homeowner lead sales
metrics: Filing-to-mailbox latency (hours)
QR scan & intake conversion % per 1,000 mailers
Annualized LTV / net revenue per mailed piece

platform_risks.failure_mode: USPS 39 U.S.C. § 3001(h)-(i) mail-stop order, State AG UDAP enforcement, or payment-processor freeze
platform_risks.trigger: Styling mailers as fake government penalty notices, invoices, or charging $89-$195 solely for a $3 public deed copy without statutory disclaimers
platform_risks.impact: Civil restitution penalties, merchant account termination, and 30%+ chargeback rates
platform_risks.detection_metric: Refund/chargeback ratio >1% and customer support inquiries mistaking the mailer for a government agency
platform_risks.fallback: Use unambiguous private commercial branding, never mimic government seals or citation numbers, and sell genuine value-add subscriptions (annual compliance updates, tax-assessment appeals, or B2B services)

plays.name: High-Velocity DM Outbound & Trigger Funnels
plays.mechanism: Replace blind cold mass-DM blasts (which die to PeerFloodError and silent Message Request graveyards) with high-velocity comment-to-DM triggers, hand-raiser reaction hooks, and multi-inbox warm signal routing.
inputs: Short-form / community trigger posts ('Comment KEYWORD')
Signal-verified prospect handles
Automated DM qualification & booking bridge
workflow: Publish high-curiosity teardown or resource posts where prospects comment a trigger keyword or react to unlock a playbook or calculator
Deliver instant automated DM replies to warm hand-raisers (bypassing cold-DM filters because the user initiated interaction) or send contextual 1-to-1 DMs referencing an active public request
Qualify budget and timeline inside a 3-message DM micro-funnel and transition immediately to a booked call, checkout link, or owned SMS/email list
metrics: Trigger-comment to DM delivery rate
DM reply-to-qualified-conversation %
Revenue per 100 DM threads

platform_risks.failure_mode: PeerFloodError, shadow-filtering into 'Hidden Requests', or link-domain blacklisting
platform_risks.trigger: Sending identical unsolicited cold DMs with raw external URLs across freshly registered or SIM-farmed accounts
platform_risks.impact: Near-0% inbox placement, outbound DM block, or permanent account suspension
platform_risks.detection_metric: Seen/reply ratio below 10% and outbound PeerFloodError / action-block frequency
platform_risks.fallback: Require user-initiated trigger action (comment/reaction/inbound message) before automated DM dispatch and send external links only after the prospect replies

plays.name: Subsidized / Developer-Tenant Multi-Inbox Cold Outbound Infrastructure
plays.mechanism: Provisioning hundreds of isolated secondary domains across subsidized Microsoft 365 developer/partner tenants, Cloudflare Email Routing, and low-cost SMTP relays—sending strictly 15–25 plain-text emails per inbox per day across 300+ free/subsidized mailboxes to deliver 150,000+ monthly B2B cold emails into primary inboxes without paying $6–$12/seat retail Google Workspace pricing.
inputs: Lookalike secondary domain portfolio with automated SPF, DKIM (2048-bit), DMARC (`p=quarantine`/`reject`), and custom tracking-free MX records
Subsidized M365 partner/developer tenants, Cloudflare Email Routing catch-alls, and distributed SMTP sending nodes
Automated peer-to-peer warmup network and master unibox reply-routing webhook
workflow: Provision 100–300 secondary sending domains and bind 2–3 mailboxes per domain via automated DNS and tenant scripts
Warm every mailbox for 14–21 days with realistic thread-depth conversations before introducing live outbound prospects
Cap daily outbound volume at <=20 zero-link, zero-tracking-pixel plain-text messages per mailbox per day to stay completely beneath ESP volume heuristics
Aggregate all prospect replies into a single unified AI-triaged inbox that books qualified B2B sales calls on pay-per-show or retainer terms
metrics: Primary-inbox placement rate (%) across Gmail and Microsoft 365 seed tests
All-in monthly infrastructure cost per 10,000 delivered plain-text emails ($)
Positive reply rate (%) and booked meetings per 1,000 prospects contacted

platform_risks.failure_mode: Tenant-wide outbound throttling or domain-footprint blacklisting (Spamhaus DBL)
platform_risks.trigger: Placing too many domains inside a single tenant, embedding tracking pixels, or exceeding 30 sends/day per mailbox
platform_risks.impact: Tenant suspension or domain-level spam-folder routing
platform_risks.detection_metric: Daily seed-list inbox placement (%) and bounce rate (<1.5% hard threshold)
platform_risks.fallback: Enforce max 2–3 domains per tenant, strip all open/click tracking pixels, verify 100% of leads via SMTP catch-all checks before sending, and keep hot-standby warmed domains ready for instant swap

plays.name: "Free LLC / Free Setup" Fintech Account Co-Registration Bounty Stacking
plays.mechanism: Offering a $0-service-fee LLC formation and business-launch concierge (borrower pays only mandatory state filing fees) that embeds a sequential post-formation 'Required Business Infrastructure Checklist' where every newly formed entity opens free business banking, corporate card, payroll, bookkeeping, and merchant accounts—yielding $600–$1,800+ in stacked B2B fintech CPA bounties per free formation.
inputs: High-intent 'free LLC formation' and 'start a business in [State]' search, social, and creator traffic
Automated state SOS filing workflow, EIN retrieval assistant, and operating-agreement generator
Direct B2B partner/CPA agreements with neobank, corporate card, payroll, and registered-agent providers
workflow: Acquire first-time founders via a genuine $0-markup LLC formation funnel where the user pays only state statutory fees
Guide the founder through an automated EIN and corporate-resolution wizard immediately upon state filing submission

Present an integrated 1-click onboarding sequence for a free business checking account ($150–$400 CPA), corporate charge card ($200–$500 CPA), payroll/bookkeeping trial ($100–$300 CPA), and web/domain host ($100–$200 CPA)
Provide automated compliance reminders and annual report tracking to capture recurring Year-2 registered-agent renewals
metrics: Stacked fintech CPA bounty revenue ($) realized per 100 free LLC formations
Post-EIN bank-account funding conversion rate (%) within 14 days of formation
Net customer acquisition margin after paid search/creator traffic spend

platform_risks.failure_mode: Fintech partner CPA clawback or payout tier downgrade due to unfunded/dormant business bank accounts
platform_risks.trigger: Sending low-intent formations that open free business bank accounts but never complete KYC or initial deposit funding
platform_risks.impact: Reversal of unvested CPA bounties or shift from account-open CPA to funded-account CPA tiers
platform_risks.detection_metric: 30-day funded-account activation rate (%) and average initial deposit balance across referred LLCs
platform_risks.fallback: Gate free operating-agreement and bookkeeping templates behind verified bank-account funding and pre-qualify founders on 30-day operating revenue intent

plays.name: Chapter 11 Bankruptcy Schedule E/F Trade-Claim & Convenience-Class Rollups
plays.mechanism: Purchase documented small trade claims below risk-adjusted expected plan distributions, accounting for objections, assignment procedures, and plan rules that may prohibit claim splitting or aggregation benefits.
inputs: Bankruptcy schedules E/F and claims register
Invoices, payment history, and assignment documents
Proposed plan classification and distribution waterfall
workflow: 1. Reconcile scheduled trade creditors with filed claims and supporting invoices
2. Model recoveries under plan amendments, objections, setoffs, and convenience-class eligibility
3. Buy eligible claims through documented assignments and complete required transfer notices
4. Monitor objections and confirmation, then reconcile distributions to each acquired claim
metrics: Purchase discount to risk-adjusted recovery
Allowed claim value versus purchased face value
Realized return and days to distribution

platform_risks.failure_mode: Claim disallowance or convenience-class exclusion
platform_risks.trigger: Disputed invoices, setoff rights, or plan restrictions on purchased or split claims
platform_risks.impact: Reduced distribution or complete capital loss
platform_risks.detection_metric: Objection rate and eligible allowed value per portfolio
platform_risks.fallback: Stop affected purchases, enforce documented seller recourse where available, and price only supported general-unsecured recoveries

plays.name: Litigation-Finance Mass-Tort Lead-to-Docket Securitization & Co-Counsel Syndicates
plays.mechanism: Pairing an Arizona Alternative Business Structure (ABS) or co-counsel law firm with an institutional litigation-finance credit facility to acquire, medically verify (via $6.50 HITECH patient-directed record requests), and package 1,000–25,000 retained mass-tort plaintiffs (PFAS, AFFF, Paraquat, NEC, rideshare assault, defective medical devices) at $1,200–$2,500 CAC—either flipping vetted case tranches to litigation-finance hedge funds at 2.5x–4x cost or holding for 35–40% global MDL settlement fee splits.
inputs: Judicial Panel on Multidistrict Litigation (JPML) docket analytics, FDA FAERS adverse-event spikes, and EPA contaminant zip-code maps
Arizona ABS / co-counsel retainer infrastructure with e-sign intake and automated HITECH Act (45 CFR § 164.524) medical-record retrieval engine
Non-recourse litigation-finance warehouse credit facility and MDL leadership co-counsel placement contracts
workflow: Identify emerging MDL mass torts with clear causation biomarkers (specific ICD-10 diagnosis codes + geographic/product exposure proof) and deep-pocket corporate defendants
Run hyper-targeted CTV, paid social, and public-record outbound campaigns to sign injured claimants directly onto joint co-counsel retainer agreements

Execute automated HITECH patient-directed electronic medical record (EMR) pulls at the federal statutory cap (~$6.50/record) and use LLM clinical parsers to verify qualifying diagnosis and exposure dates within 72 hours

Securitize verified, deficiency-free case tranches into litigation-finance buyout facilities at $4,500–$9,000 per vetted retainer or hold on the balance sheet for $25,000–$80,000+ gross contingency fees at MDL settlement
metrics: All-in cost per medically verified, deficiency-free retained plaintiff ($1,200–$2,500)
HITECH medical-record retrieval turnaround time (hours) and clinical qualification pass rate (%)
Secondary docket tranche sale multiple (2.5x–4.0x CAC) or net MDL settlement IRR

platform_risks.fallback: Diversify docket holdings across 6–10 uncorrelated mass torts and single-event commercial casualty niches, pay media vendors strictly on EMR-verified retainers, and offload 50% of tranche cost basis early to institutional litigation funders

platform_risks.trigger: Hidden commissions, inaccurate balances, or new financing breaching existing contracts
platform_risks.impact: Accelerated collections and broker liability
platform_risks.detection_metric: Undisclosed fee exceptions and covenant breaches per engagement
platform_risks.fallback: Stop placement, refund improper fees, and refer the merchant to independent licensed restructuring counsel
platform_risks.play_name: MCA UCC-1 Trigger Stacking & Dual-Sided Default-Restructure Brokerage

platform_risks.failure_mode: Portal rate-limiting or CAPTCHA gating
platform_risks.trigger: High-frequency automated polling against county or agency web portals
platform_risks.impact: Delayed lead ingestion or temporary IP block on target registry
platform_risks.detection_metric: HTTP 429/403 rate and daily record ingestion delta
platform_risks.fallback: Switch to scheduled bulk FOIA/public-record exports, official data feeds, and low-frequency cached queues

platform_risks.failure_mode: USPS 39 U.S.C. § 3001(h)-(i) mail-stop order, State AG UDAP enforcement, or payment-processor freeze
platform_risks.trigger: Styling mailers as fake government penalty notices, invoices, or charging $89-$195 solely for a $3 public deed copy without statutory disclaimers
platform_risks.impact: Civil restitution penalties, merchant account termination, and 30%+ chargeback rates
platform_risks.detection_metric: Refund/chargeback ratio >1% and customer support inquiries mistaking the mailer for a government agency
platform_risks.fallback: Use unambiguous private commercial branding, never mimic government seals or citation numbers, and sell genuine value-add subscriptions (annual compliance updates, tax-assessment appeals, or B2B services)

platform_risks.failure_mode: PeerFloodError, shadow-filtering into 'Hidden Requests', or link-domain blacklisting
platform_risks.trigger: Sending identical unsolicited cold DMs with raw external URLs across freshly registered or SIM-farmed accounts
platform_risks.impact: Near-0% inbox placement, outbound DM block, or permanent account suspension
platform_risks.detection_metric: Seen/reply ratio below 10% and outbound PeerFloodError / action-block frequency
platform_risks.fallback: Require user-initiated trigger action (comment/reaction/inbound message) before automated DM dispatch and send external links only after the prospect replies

platform_risks.failure_mode: Tenant-wide outbound throttling or domain-footprint blacklisting (Spamhaus DBL)
platform_risks.trigger: Placing too many domains inside a single tenant, embedding tracking pixels, or exceeding 30 sends/day per mailbox
platform_risks.impact: Tenant suspension or domain-level spam-folder routing
platform_risks.detection_metric: Daily seed-list inbox placement (%) and bounce rate (<1.5% hard threshold)
platform_risks.fallback: Enforce max 2–3 domains per tenant, strip all open/click tracking pixels, verify 100% of leads via SMTP catch-all checks before sending, and keep hot-standby warmed domains ready for instant swap
platform_risks.play_name: Subsidized / Developer-Tenant Multi-Inbox Cold Outbound Infrastructure

platform_risks.failure_mode: Fintech partner CPA clawback or payout tier downgrade due to unfunded/dormant business bank accounts
platform_risks.trigger: Sending low-intent formations that open free business bank accounts but never complete KYC or initial deposit funding
platform_risks.impact: Reversal of unvested CPA bounties or shift from account-open CPA to funded-account CPA tiers
platform_risks.detection_metric: 30-day funded-account activation rate (%) and average initial deposit balance across referred LLCs
platform_risks.fallback: Gate free operating-agreement and bookkeeping templates behind verified bank-account funding and pre-qualify founders on 30-day operating revenue intent
platform_risks.play_name: "Free LLC / Free Setup" Fintech Account Co-Registration Bounty Stacking

platform_risks.failure_mode: Claim disallowance or convenience-class exclusion
platform_risks.trigger: Disputed invoices, setoff rights, or plan restrictions on purchased or split claims
platform_risks.impact: Reduced distribution or complete capital loss
platform_risks.detection_metric: Objection rate and eligible allowed value per portfolio
platform_risks.fallback: Stop affected purchases, enforce documented seller recourse where available, and price only supported general-unsecured recoveries
platform_risks.play_name: Chapter 11 Bankruptcy Schedule E/F Trade-Claim & Convenience-Class Rollups

platform_risks.failure_mode: Daubert general-causation dismissal in the MDL or fraudulent duplicate claimant intake
platform_risks.trigger: Federal MDL judge excluding plaintiff expert witnesses under Rule 702 or lead vendors submitting synthetic/dual-represented claimants
platform_risks.impact: Write-down of single-tort docket value or MDL leadership rejecting duplicate retainers
platform_risks.detection_metric: Real-time SSN/lexis duplicate-retainer cross-check, immediate HITECH EMR verification before media payout, and max 20% capital concentration in any single MDL
platform_risks.fallback: Diversify docket holdings across 6–10 uncorrelated mass torts and single-event commercial casualty niches, pay media vendors strictly on EMR-verified retainers, and offload 50% of tranche cost basis early to institutional litigation funders
platform_risks.play_name: Litigation-Finance Mass-Tort Lead-to-Docket Securitization & Co-Counsel Syndicates
